title: Australian Postal Corporation (Unsolicited Political Communications) Bill 2016
short_title: Australian Postal Corporation (Unsolicited Political Communications) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would stop Australia Post delivering unaddressed political material to premises displaying specified signs rejecting unaddressed mail or political material, or accepting addressed mail only.
It would make specified delivery preferences binding by adding a restriction to the Australian Postal Corporation Act that applies when Australia Post supplies unaddressed mail.
The restriction would apply through Australia Post’s unaddressed mail service and cover material from or about registered parties, federal election candidates, House members and senators.
changes: Specified signs or stickers would trigger a prohibition on unaddressed political deliveries.
The restriction would not apply where it infringes constitutional political communication protections or acquires property without just terms.
The substantive postal amendment would begin on 1 July 2017.
summary.affected: Australia Post, people displaying the specified signs, registered political parties, federal candidates, House members and senators are affected.
